newsitem.title: TURKEY: Coalition ally says Turkey's Erbakan to quit.
newsitem.headline: Coalition ally says Turkey's Erbakan to quit.

text.p: Turkey's junior coalition partner said on Monday that Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan would resign this week in a power-sharing deal to end a row over Islamist activism.

"In the next one or two days, the 54th government will come to an end, Erbakan will resign. In such an environment, the thing to do is to form an election government," Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller told a business group meeting.
Erbakan and Ciller, head of the pro-Western True Path Party, earlier announced they would swap jobs by the end of this month and form a caretaker government to go for early elections.

But the planned power transfer and early polls would have to overcome the serious obstacles of presidential and parliamentary approval. The coalition lacks a majority in the national assembly after a series of defections.

The government, the 54th to rule Turkey since the country was established as a secularist state in the 1920s, has been under intense pressure in recent months in an anti-Islamist campaign, led by the secularist army.
Ciller says she could ward off the army better than Erbakan if she were made prime minister.

One of Ciller's aides gave a day for the prime minister's resignation. "Erbakan will resign on Wednesday in line with the coalition protocol," Anatolian news agency quoted True Path deputy chairman Hasan Ekinci as saying.
Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, declined at a news conference on Monday to fix a date for the handover.
